{
 "cells": [
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a5bd3090",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Performing deDANSy on an RNA-sequencing dataset (Shimpi & Tan et al. 2021)\n",
    "\n",
    "Note: This come directly from the supplementary file provided with the publication. This is based on a RNA-sequencing dataset which requires converting between ENSEMBL gene IDs to UniProt IDs."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 1,
   "id": "93937489",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "import pandas as pd\n",
    "import numpy as np\n",
    "import networkx as nx\n",
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n",
    "from pybiomart import Dataset\n",
    "\n",
    "import dansy"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 2,
   "id": "62a6977a",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# First need to import and create an ID conversion dataframe\n",
    "bm_dataset = Dataset(host = 'http://useast.ensembl.org', name='hsapiens_gene_ensembl',)\n",
    "gene_ID_conv = bm_dataset.query(attributes=['ensembl_gene_id','external_gene_name','uniprotswissprot'])\n",
    "\n",
    "# Importing the proteome reference file\n",
    "ref,_ = dansy.import_proteome_files(ref_file_dir='../', reference_file_suffix='Jan7_2025.csv')"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 3,
   "id": "42da93e0",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Now importing the data of interest\n",
    "input_dir = './'\n",
    "filename = 'Shimpi_Tan_RNA_seq_Results.csv'\n",
    "data = pd.read_csv(input_dir+filename)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 4,
   "id": "dfca9da7",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Starting to fetch n-grams.\n",
      "Finished getting all n-grams\n",
      "Starting to generate adjacency\n",
      "Finished building adjacency.\n",
      "Building the reference network information.\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Now building the deDANSy object\n",
    "my_dedansy = dansy.DEdansy(uniprot_ref = ref, \n",
    "                           dataset=data,\n",
    "                            id_conv=gene_ID_conv,\n",
    "                            conv_cols = 'Gene stable ID',\n",
    "                            data_ids = 'ensembl_gene_id')\n",
    "\n",
    "# And now creating the metadata for designating differentially expressed genes\n",
    "my_dedansy.create_contrast_metadata(comparisons = ['HAS2_v_Control','HAS3_v_Control'],\n",
    "                                    fc_cols = ['log2FoldChange_HAS2','log2FoldChange_HAS3'],\n",
    "                                    pval_cols = ['padj_HAS2','padj_HAS3'],\n",
    "                                    fcs = 1,\n",
    "                                    alphas = 0.05)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "c4429509",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 300x300 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# The deDANSy object now has several built-in functions that allow for quick visualization of the n-gram network colored by whether n-grams are associated with up- or down-regulated genes.\n",
    "\n",
    "# Setting up the DEG condition\n",
    "my_dedansy.calc_DEG_ngrams('HAS2_v_Control')\n",
    "\n",
    "# Now establishing the layout of the network and then visualizing\n",
    "pos = nx.spring_layout(my_dedansy.G, k = 0.04, seed = 123)\n",
    "my_dedansy.plot_DEG_ns(pos=pos)\n",
    "plt.gcf().set_size_inches(1,1)\n",
    "plt.gcf().set_dpi(300)\n"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 6,
   "id": "4fa86846",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 300x300 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# If you only want to focus on the largest connected component:\n",
    "my_dedansy.plot_DEG_ns(pos=pos, large_cc_mode=True)\n",
    "plt.gcf().set_size_inches(1,1)\n",
    "plt.gcf().set_dpi(300)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "fae372b6",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "While visualizing the network provides an initial assessment of how distinct n-grams from each condition are, to get a more quantitative value we can calculate the separation and distinction scores from the actual deDANSy algorithm."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 7,
   "id": "f941bdf0",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "2025-08-05 15:35:37:.....Starting deDANSy scoring analysis with random seed: 123\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:35:51:.....Done with enrichment-based pruning for HAS2_v_Control\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:36:11:.....Done with enrichment-based pruning for HAS3_v_Control\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:36:11:.....Starting the false positive rate procedure.\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:37:08:.....Finished FPR procedure for HAS2_v_Control.\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:38:25:.....Finished FPR procedure for HAS3_v_Control.\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:38:25:.....Preparing the FPR results for export\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# The algorithm can be run on multiple conditions in one round\n",
    "my_dedansy.calculate_scores(comps = ['HAS2_v_Control', 'HAS3_v_Control'],\n",
    "                            num_ss_trials=20, # Lower than recommended to save time (Default value of 100 is recommended)\n",
    "                            fpr_trials=5, # Lower than recommended to save time (Default value of 50 is recommended)\n",
    "                            min_pval=-10,\n",
    "                            processes=8,\n",
    "                            seed=123, # For reproducibility but can be omitted\n",
    "                            verbose=True)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "bd6a474e",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 450x200 with 2 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# We can then display each of the scores as a bubble plot\n",
    "axs = my_dedansy.plot_scores(aspect=5) # The aspect parameter changes the aspect ratio which can make the graph a bit more aesthetically pleasing.\n",
    "plt.gcf().set_dpi(100)\n",
    "plt.gcf().set_size_inches(4.5,2)"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "a32bd51b",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "## Running additional comparisons after scores have been generated\n",
    "\n",
    "Sometimes, you may want to add in additional comparisons, which are either additional biological comparisons not explored, or to be more restrictive in what is designated as a differentially expressed gene/protein. You can add in additional comparisons after scores have been calculated and then run a second time with new comparisons to allow additional analysis to be conducted."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 11,
   "id": "c3bdd35b",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "2025-08-05 15:38:42:.....Starting deDANSy scoring analysis with random seed: 123\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:38:54:.....Done with enrichment-based pruning for HAS2_restrictive\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:39:10:.....Done with enrichment-based pruning for HAS3_restrictive\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:39:10:.....Starting the false positive rate procedure.\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:40:04:.....Finished FPR procedure for HAS2_restrictive.\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:41:14:.....Finished FPR procedure for HAS3_restrictive.\n",
      "2025-08-05 15:41:14:.....Preparing the FPR results for export\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "my_dedansy.create_contrast_metadata(comparisons = ['HAS2_restrictive', 'HAS3_restrictive'],\n",
    "                                    fc_cols = ['log2FoldChange_HAS2','log2FoldChange_HAS3'],\n",
    "                                    pval_cols = ['padj_HAS2','padj_HAS3'],\n",
    "                                    fcs = 1,\n",
    "                                    alphas = 0.001)\n",
    "my_dedansy.calculate_scores(comps = ['HAS2_restrictive', 'HAS3_restrictive'],\n",
    "                            num_ss_trials=20, # Lower than recommended to save time (Default value of 100 is recommended)\n",
    "                            fpr_trials=5, # Lower than recommended to save time (Default value of 50 is recommended)\n",
    "                            min_pval=-10,\n",
    "                            processes=8,\n",
    "                            seed=123, # For reproducibility but can be omitted\n",
    "                            verbose=True)\n"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "717af17a",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Determining the enriched n-grams of individual conditions.\n",
    "\n",
    "In addition to generating scores for network wide behavior, deDANSy can get the significantly enriched n-grams for both up- and down-regulated proteins/genes. Like how DANSy collapses n-grams representing similar data, the n-gram enrichment calculation collapses n-grams that have similar significance values that have a parent-children relationship (i.e. shorter n-gram in a longer n-gram)."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 5,
   "id": "a5387281",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "my_dedansy.calculate_ngram_enrichment('HAS2_v_Control')\n",
    "my_dedansy.plot_ngram_enrichment('HAS2_v_Control')\n",
    "\n",
    "# And just like before can adjust the aspect ratio to make it a little more aesthetically pleasing.\n",
    "plt.gca().set_aspect(.5)\n",
    "plt.title('HAS2_v_Control')\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "0a53afe0",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "Each comparison can have its own plot to show the unique/shared n-grams for each comparison."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 8,
   "id": "5bd606ab",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Will be overwriting existing DEG data.\n"
     ]
    },
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "my_dedansy.calculate_ngram_enrichment('HAS3_v_Control')\n",
    "my_dedansy.plot_ngram_enrichment('HAS3_v_Control')\n",
    "\n",
    "# And just like before can adjust the aspect ratio to make it a little more aesthetically pleasing.\n",
    "plt.gca().set_aspect(.5)\n",
    "plt.title('HAS3_v_Control')\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "7cd7aa1e",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "The displayed n-grams can be adjusted to pass a more lenient/restrictive cutoff for being displayed. We can use either a p-value cutoff (p parameter) or a quantile cutoff (q parameter) to change the plot behavior."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 9,
   "id": "72379ab5",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "data": {
      "image/png": "",
      "text/plain": [
       "<Figure size 640x480 with 1 Axes>"
      ]
     },
     "metadata": {},
     "output_type": "display_data"
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "my_dedansy.plot_ngram_enrichment('HAS3_v_Control',q=0.01)\n",
    "plt.gca().set_aspect(2)\n",
    "plt.title('HAS3_v_Control\\nOnly Top 1%')\n",
    "plt.show()"
   ]
  },

  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "aa70c564",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "# Performing deDANSy analysis with (phospho-)proteomic data\n",
    "\n",
    "If you are working with a proteomic dataset and do not require converting IDs because you are using UniProt IDs, you can build a deDANSy object without the conversion and perform analysis as outlined below with a phosphoproteomic dataset from [Chen et al, 2024](https://doi.org/10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-23-0218). We are using Supplementary Table S5 specifically."
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": null,
   "id": "41cf0123",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [],
   "source": [
    "# Importing the data\n",
    "filename = 'CUTO28_pY_Results.xlsx'\n",
    "raw_phos = pd.read_excel(filename,header=1)\n",
    "\n",
    "# First filtering out the raw data to ensure we only have the human data and those found within our reference file.\n",
    "proc_phos = raw_phos[raw_phos['IsHuman'] == 1]\n",
    "proc_phos = proc_phos[proc_phos['Protein'].isin(ref['UniProt ID'])]"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "code",
   "execution_count": 14,
   "id": "d144ca71",
   "metadata": {},
   "outputs": [
    {
     "name": "stdout",
     "output_type": "stream",
     "text": [
      "Starting to fetch n-grams.\n",
      "Finished getting all n-grams\n",
      "Starting to generate adjacency\n",
      "Finished building adjacency.\n",
      "Building the reference network information.\n"
     ]
    }
   ],
   "source": [
    "# Now building the deDANSy object, which can ignore any ID conversion by setting the run_conversion parameter to False.\n",
    "prot_dedansy = dansy.DEdansy(dataset = proc_phos,\n",
    "                             uniprot_ref = ref,\n",
    "                             data_ids = 'Protein',\n",
    "                             run_conversion = False)"
   ]
  },
  {
   "cell_type": "markdown",
   "id": "774f1a33",
   "metadata": {},
   "source": [
    "After this the process of calculating scores and plotting them is identical."
   ]
  }
